# Citation

Frazee, A. C., et al. (2015). *Polyester: simulating RNA-seq datasets with differential transcript expression*. Bioinformatics. DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv272. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4635655/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4635655/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Introduces Polyester for simulation of RNA-seq reads with transcript-level differential expression and replicate-aware count generation.

# Scope for simitall

Use as a sequencing-read layer after simitall generates sample-level expression truth. Keep biological expression effects and technical FASTQ simulation as separate, traceable stages.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Read simulation should start from a declared transcriptome and expression design.
- Replicates, condition effects, and transcript-level effects should be saved as truth metadata.
- Count-level and FASTQ-level simulations answer different benchmarking questions.

# Inputs to Specify

- Transcript sequences or annotation
- Sample-level expression design
- Read and fragment settings

# Expected Outputs

- Simulated RNA-seq reads
- Expression or count truth
- Replicate and condition metadata

# Limitations and Guardrails

- FASTQ realism depends on the chosen transcriptome and technical parameters.
- Polyester alone does not create genotype-linked eQTL architecture.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- How should simulated GWAS genotypes be connected to RNA-seq expression truth?
- When are read-level RNA-seq outputs necessary instead of a count matrix?
